arxiv-1705-05512.title: Cooperative Learning with Visual Attributes
arxiv-1705-05512.creator: Tanmay BatraCarnegie Mellon University tbatra@cmu.edu, Devi ParikhGeorgia Tech parikh@gatech.edu
arxiv-1705-05512.description: Abstract Learning paradigms involving varying levels of supervision have received a lot of interest within the computer vision and machine learning communities. The supervisory information is typically considered to come from a human supervisor – a “teacher” figure. In this paper, we consider an alternate source of supervision – a “peer” – i.e . a different machine.

arxiv-2104-02645.title: Improved simulation of beam backgrounds and collimation at SuperKEKB
arxiv-2104-02645.creator: A. Natochii, S. E. Vahsen, H. Nakayama, T. Ishibashi, S. Terui
arxiv-2104-02645.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by A. Natochii, S. E. Vahsen, H. Nakayama, T. Ishibashi, S. Terui. Mitigation of beam backgrounds via collimators is critical for the success of the Belle II experiment at the SuperKEKB electron-positron collider. We report on an improved simulation methodology, which includes a refined physical description of the collimators and beam pipe, our first implementation of collimator tip scattering, and in which the existing beam particle tracking software has been embedded into a new sequential tracking framework.

arxiv-2202-11297.title: Minimum time trajectory planning for surveying using UAVs
arxiv-2202-11297.creator: Srinath Tankasala, Can Pehlivanturk, Mitch Pryor
arxiv-2202-11297.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a motion planning strategy for UAVs that generates a time-optimal trajectory to survey a given target area. There are several situations where completing an aerial survey is time sensitive, such as gaining situational awareness for first responders, surveying hazardous environments, etc.

arxiv-2203-17009.title: Assessing the performance of quantum annealing with nonlinear driving
arxiv-2203-17009.creator: Artur Soriani, Pierre Nazé, Marcus V. S. Bonança, Bartłomiej Gardas, Sebastian Deffner
arxiv-2203-17009.description: Abstract Current generation quantum annealers have already proven to be successful problem-solvers. Yet, quantum annealing is still very much in its infancy, with suboptimal applicability. For instance, to date it is still an open question which annealing protocol causes the fewest diabatic excitations for a given eigenspectrum, and even whether there is a universally optimal strategy.

arxiv-2510-01373.title: Detection of OH maser emission in the 71-year periodic comet 12P/Pons–Brooks using the 40-m Thai National Radio Telescope (TNRT) Facilities: COBS Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) ; emcee ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 )
arxiv-2510-01373.creator: Nobuyuki Sakai, Saran Poshyachinda, Koichiro Sugiyama, Wiphu Rujopakarn, Boonrucksar Soonthornthum, Apichat Leckngam, Busaba H. Kramer, Phrudth Jaroenjittichai, Bannawit Pimpanuwat, Dan Singwong, Kitipoom Kanjana, Nikom Prasert, Songklod Punyawarin, Spiro George Sarris, Teep Chairin, Kamorn Bandudej
arxiv-2510-01373.description: Abstract Although the optical cometary database is extensive, the radio database is limited. The 18-cm OH maser observations of comets allow us to determine (i) the production rate of OH ( Q OH Q_{\rm{OH}} ) and (ii) the water expansion velocity, for each comet.

arxiv-2512-11213.title: FutureWeaver : Planning Test-Time Compute for Multi-Agent Systems with Modularized Collaboration
arxiv-2512-11213.creator: Dongwon Jung, Peng Shi, Yi Zhang
arxiv-2512-11213.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dongwon Jung, Peng Shi, Yi Zhang. Scaling test-time computation improves large language model performance without additional training. Recent work demonstrates that techniques such as repeated sampling, self-verification, and self-reflection can significantly enhance task success by allocating more inference-time compute. However, applying these techniques across multiple agents in a multi-agent system is difficult: there does not exist principled mechanisms to allocate compute to foster collaboration among agents, to extend test-time scaling to collaborative interactions, or to distribute compute across agents under explicit budget constraints.

arxiv-2601-20694.title: Is Pure Exploitation Sufficient in Exogenous MDPs with Linear Function Approximation?
arxiv-2601-20694.creator: Hao Liang, Jiayu Cheng, Sean R. Sinclair, Yali Du
arxiv-2601-20694.description: Abstract Exogenous MDPs (Exo-MDPs) capture sequential decision-making where uncertainty comes solely from exogenous inputs that evolve independently of the learner’s actions. This structure is especially common in operations research applications such as inventory control, energy storage, and resource allocation, where exogenous randomness (e.g., demand, arrivals, or prices) drives system behavior.

arxiv-2601-22902.title: Evidence for quark-diquark structure of baryons from fluctuations of conserved charges
arxiv-2601-22902.creator: Michał Marczenko, Krzysztof Redlich
arxiv-2601-22902.description: Abstract We study fluctuations and correlations of conserved charges in QCD using a string-based description of the hadronic mass spectrum. Mesons and baryons are modeled as open relativistic strings with quark-antiquark and quark-diquark endpoints, respectively, leading to an exponential Hagedorn growth of states with a limiting temperature fixed by the string tension.

arxiv-2604-28004.title: Minimal Parametric Networks in Hyperspaces and their Properties
arxiv-2604-28004.creator: Arsen Galstyan

pmc-10743123.title: The Use of Predictive Microbiology for the Prediction of the Shelf Life of Food Products
pmc-10743123.creator: Fatih Tarlak, Arun K Bhunia
pmc-10743123.description: Microbial shelf life refers to the duration of time during which a food product remains safe for consumption in terms of its microbiological quality. Predictive microbiology is a field of science that focuses on using mathematical models and computational techniques to predict the growth, survival, and behaviour of microorganisms in food and other environments.

pmc-11299250.title: Characteristics of CYP3A4-related potential drug-drug interactions in outpatients receiving prescriptions from multiple clinical departments
pmc-11299250.creator: Rina Matsuoka, Shinsuke Akagi, Tomohiro Konishi, Masashi Kondo, Hideki Matsubara, Shohei Yamamoto, Keiji Izushi, Yuichi Tasaka
pmc-11299250.description: BackgroundDrug-drug interactions (DDIs) increase the incidence of adverse drug reactions (ADRs). In a previous report, we revealed that the incidence of potential DDIs due to the same CYP molecular species in one prescription exceeds 90% among patients taking six or more drugs and that CYP3A4 markedly influences the increase in the number of potential DDIs in clinical practice.

pmc-11433843.title: Nanomedicine in Neuroprotection, Neuroregeneration, and Blood–Brain Barrier Modulation: A Narrative Review
pmc-11433843.creator: Antea Krsek, Ana Jagodic, Lara Baticic, Edgaras Stankevičius, Zbigniew Żuber, Katarzyna Fischer, Bogdan Batko
pmc-11433843.description: Nanomedicine is a newer, promising approach to promote neuroprotection, neuroregeneration, and modulation of the blood–brain barrier. This review includes the integration of various nanomaterials in neurological disorders. In addition, gelatin-based hydrogels, which have huge potential due to biocompatibility, maintenance of porosity, and enhanced neural process outgrowth, are reviewed.

pmc-11438477.title: Resources for innovative learning of anatomy and foot ossification: Graphic design and virtual reality
pmc-11438477.creator: Ana Cristina Moreno‐Marin, Manuel Pardo Rios, Eva Lopezosa‐Reca, Cristina Molina García, Salvador Díaz‐Miguel, Beatriz Gómez‐Martín, Paula Cobos‐Moreno
pmc-11438477.description: IntroductionThis study addresses the ossification process of the foot, a topic of great relevance within podiatry courses. Understanding the chronology of foot bone formation is essential for evaluating pathological processes and establishing appropriate therapeutic actions to improve patient quality of life.

pmc-11517019.title: Methods to Handle Missing depression (PHQ-8 Score) Values among Adults in the United Arab Emirates
pmc-11517019.creator: M Al Balushi, A Ahmad, S Javaid, M Grivna, F Al Maskari, S Sherman, A Abdulle, F Piano, R Ali
pmc-11517019.description: BackgroundThe UAE Healthy Future Study (UAEHFS) is one of the first large prospective cohort studies in the Gulf region which examines causes and risk factors for chronic diseases among adult UAE nationals. Missing values are often unavoidable in empirical research and can in many cases, lead to bias.

pmc-11574197.title: Cognitive reorganization in patients with Parkinson’s Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment: a neuropsychological network approach
pmc-11574197.creator: Chiara Longo, Daniele Luigi Romano, Maria Chiara Malaguti, Ruggero Bacchin, Costanza Papagno
pmc-11574197.description: Parkinson’s Disease (PD) exhibits heterogeneous cognitive deficits that may represent different cognitive phenotypes. While previous studies have described them in a “macro” manner, only one study has applied Network Analysis (NA) in PD. NA represents a model to explore relationships between cognitive abilities, aiding in understanding cognitive phenotypes.

pmc-11615382.title: The influence of core-build up materials on biaxial flexural strength of strength-gradient zirconia and lithium disilicate ceramics: an in-vitro study
pmc-11615382.creator: Nadia S. Ereifej, Dina B. Musa, Yara G. Oweis, Motasum Abu-Awwad, Abedelmalek K. Tabnjh
pmc-11615382.description: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of using different core build-up materials on biaxial flexural strength (BFS) of multilayered strength-gradient zirconia ceramic in comparison to lithium disilicate ceramic. Thirty zirconia discs were fabricated from IPS e.max ZirCAD Prime (Zir), 30 discs from IPS e.

pmc-11734029.title: Percutaneous Removal of Cardiac Papillary Fibroelastomas
pmc-11734029.creator: Robert Seby, Goyal Umadat, Samantha Espinosa, Prajwal Reddy, Pragnesh Parikh, Jordan Ray, Melanie C. Bois, S. Michael Gharacholou, Kyle W. Klarich, Abdallah El Sabbagh
pmc-11734029.description: Papillary fibroelastomas (PFEs) are primary cardiac tumors associated with significant embolic risk. Surgical excision or medical therapy with antiplatelets and/or anticoagulants have been the treatment options for symptomatic patients. This paper reports our early experiences of percutaneous removal of PFE using mechanical aspiration techniques.

pmc-12492940.title: Effects of isolated gastrocnemius tightness on foot posture, strength, function, and balance in children aged 7–16: a case-control study
pmc-12492940.creator: Fatma Eren-Zengin, Deniz Tuncer, Hakan Senaran, Gokcer Uzer
pmc-12492940.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIsolated gastrocnemius tightness (IGT) has been linked to foot conditions, but its clinical relevance in children remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate foot posture, muscle strength, functional performance, and postural control in children with IGT.MethodsFourteen children diagnosed with IGT, defined as having passive ankle dorsiflexion < 10° with the knee extended and ≥ 10° with the knee flexed according to the Silfverskiold test, and 14 age-matched children without IGT were included in the study.

pmc-12606745.title: Spheroid-Based 3D Models to Decode Cell Function and Matrix Effectors in Breast Cancer
pmc-12606745.creator: Sylvia Mangani, Christos Koutsakis, Nikolaos E. Koletsis, Zoi Piperigkou, Marco Franchi, Martin Götte, Nikos K. Karamanos
pmc-12606745.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryTraditional two-dimensional (2D) cell cultures are widely used in cancer research but fail to replicate the complex interactions that occur in tumors in vivo. Three-dimensional (3D) models more closely mimic the tumor microenvironment by preserving dynamic cell–matrix communication. In this study, we developed and characterized 3D spheroids from two breast cancer cell lines with distinct metastatic potential (MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231). Significant differences in cell morphology, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers expression, and functional behavior compared to 2D cultures were observed.

pmc-12619460.title: LTCONS_00014107-miR-29b-2-3p-GPR37 axis promotes heat stimulation induced esophageal carcinogenesis
pmc-12619460.creator: Wenting Liu, Jiaping Qu, Jing Wang, Li He, Dan Cheng, Jiaqiong Li, Yiu To Yeung, Liting Zhou, Yunfeng Gao, Hui Huang, Zigang Dong, Xiang Li
pmc-12619460.description: Esophageal cancer is a common malignant tumor of the digestive system, and Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is the major histological subtype of esophageal cancer. Multiple epidemiological evidence shows that consumption of hot temperature food and beverages is an important risk factor for developing ESCC, however, its underlying mechanism remains unclear.

pmc-13156469.title: FBXW7‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Mechanisms, and Tumor Predisposition
pmc-13156469.creator: S Savasta, F F Comisi, E Fiumicelli, G B Dell’Isola, G Di Pasquale, G D Mangano, L Zagaroli, V Salpietro, A Verrotti, Harleen Khatra
pmc-13156469.description: F‐box and WD repeat domain‐containing 7 (FBXW7) encodes the substrate‐recognition subunit of the SCF (SKP1‐CUL1‐F‐box) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, where it regulates proteasome‐mediated degradation of key cell cycle and developmental proteins. The aim of this review is to provide a comprehensive overview of the currently available evidence on the clinical and molecular features of FBXW7‐related neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD).

pmc-13676376.title: Differential requirements for cytokine signaling and local antigen in upper versus lower respiratory tract CD8+ TRM development
pmc-13676376.creator: Kirsten K Rodgers, Mark Elliott Williams, Ariana R Jimenez, Sakeenah L Hicks, Cameron L R Mattingly, Sarah E Michalets, Yixel M Soto-Vázquez, Kathryn M Moore, Madeleine M Rasche, Laurel A Lawrence, Yu-shan Huang, Thien Duy Chen, Sofia R Cendoya, Christopher D Scharer, Alison Swaims-Kohlmeier, Jacob
pmc-13676376.description: CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM) in the upper respiratory tract (URT) limit viral replication after transmission and prevent spread to the lower respiratory tract (LRT), whereas LRT CD8+ TRM are important for limiting immunopathology in the lung and promoting efficient viral clearance.

pmc-13682454.title: Mechanism-guided endograft explantation eliminates shear-mediated aortic injury in a controlled simulation study
pmc-13682454.creator: Zain Moin, Alayne Morrel, Maham Rahimi
pmc-13682454.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveEndograft explantation is associated with high morbidity and mortality, driven in part by uncontrolled shear-mediated aortic injury. In this study, we evaluated whether a mechanism-based explantation device could reduce this injury and improve the procedural performance.MethodsIn a controlled simulation using a multilayered three-dimensional printed aortic model, 25 vascular trainees and surgeons performed endograft explantation using both a conventional syringe technique and a novel device (EndoEx).
